road.title: What you did
road.description: A round and unhurried shape in a uniform that belongs to a different job, next to a small bell marked RING FOR ATTENTION and a larger one marked DO NOT. Lazlo is a Alibi Notary and certifies what people were doing at the time, in triplicate, for a modest fee.

openObjectives.prompt: Lazlo is entering yesterday in a ledger and has got as far as lunch. Tell Lazlo what you ate or drank yesterday, using Italian.
Lazlo has noticed that you are carrying more than you set out with. Tell Lazlo something that you bought, using Italian.

character.name: Lazlo Nettlebed
character.description: A round and unhurried shape in a uniform that belongs to a different job, next to a small bell marked RING FOR ATTENTION and a larger one marked DO NOT. Lazlo is a Alibi Notary and certifies what people were doing at the time, in triplicate, for a modest fee.

npc.narrative: You reach The Occasional Common at alba, sotto un cielo senza nuvole. Lazlo Nettlebed stands in a fila of one, beside a small tavolo, holding a pen, a form and a biscotto he has not yet decided to give away.
npc.native: Buongiorno! Ieri ho mangiato una mela e ho bevuto un tè, in triplice copia. Io sono Lazlo, il notaio. E tu, come stai questa mattina?
npc.translation: Good morning! Yesterday I ate an apple and I drank a tea, in triplicate. I am Lazlo, the notary. And you, how are you this morning?

player: Sto bene, grazie! Ieri ho mangiato una pizza e ho bevuto due caffè. Troppo caffè!

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely answer! You said how you are and told Lazlo about your pizza and your two coffees, all in correct Italian.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done: you told Lazlo what you ate and drank yesterday, with "Ieri ho mangiato" and "ho bevuto".
Not yet: this one needs you to tell Lazlo something you bought. Lazlo will ask about it again later.
Not yet: this one needs you to tell Lazlo one thing that happened last week. Lazlo will ask about it again later.

openObjectives.prompt: Lazlo has noticed that you are carrying more than you set out with. Tell Lazlo something that you bought, using Italian.
Lazlo is a week behind and is relying on you for the whole of it. Tell Lazlo one thing that happened last week, using Italian.

npc.narrative: Lazlo writes your due caffè on a modulo, in triplicate, and slides a piccolo biscotto across the tavolo. Behind you the fila consists of you, which he seems to find correct. He stamps the carta once, piano, as if it might object.
npc.native: Bene, sono contento! Due caffè sono troppi per un notaio, ma tu sei forte. Io ho comprato un timbro nuovo. E tu, che cosa hai comprato?
npc.translation: Good, I am glad! Two coffees are too many for a notary, but you are strong. I bought a new stamp. And you, what did you buy?

player: Ho comprato un ombrello, ma oggi non piove! Perché un timbro nuovo?

verdict.overallFeedback: Great job telling Lazlo you bought an umbrella, and you even asked him a question back! Next, try telling him about something from last week.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done: you used "Ho comprato un ombrello" correctly to say what you bought.
You didn't mention last week yet; tell Lazlo one thing that happened last week. Lazlo will ask again later.

openObjectives.prompt: Lazlo is a week behind and is relying on you for the whole of it. Tell Lazlo one thing that happened last week, using Italian.

npc.narrative: Lazlo looks at your ombrello with great rispetto, then at the cielo, which is clear and entirely without a nuvola. He forms a queue of one in front of the tavolo and offers a piccolo biscotto, keeping a thumb on it.
npc.native: Un ombrello, bene! Oggi non piove, ma un ombrello è sempre pronto. Il timbro vecchio è rotto, e la settimana scorsa ho fatto un errore. E tu, che cosa hai fatto la settimana scorsa?
npc.translation: An umbrella, good! Today it is not raining, but an umbrella is always ready. The old stamp is broken, and last week I made a mistake. And you, what did you do last week?

player: La settimana scorsa sono andato a Roma con mia sorella. Era molto caldo. Che errore hai fatto?

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely answer! You told Lazlo about your trip to Rome with your sister, said it was hot, and asked him a question back.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done: you used "La settimana scorsa" correctly to say what happened last week.

vocabularyEvidence.evidence: La settimana scorsa sono andato a Roma con mia sorella.

npc.narrative: Lazlo puts down his penna and studies the modulo with grande rispetto. The cielo is clear, the alba is quiet, and the coda behind you is empty, which does not stop him. From a cassetto he takes one piccolo biscotto.
npc.native: Roma con tua sorella, che bello! Io ho scritto martedì, ma era mercoledì, e l'alibi era sbagliato. Ecco un biscotto: il tuo viaggio è ufficiale. Che cosa hai mangiato a Roma?
npc.translation: Rome with your sister, how lovely! I wrote Tuesday, but it was Wednesday, and the alibi was wrong. Here is a biscuit: your trip is official. What did you eat in Rome?

player: A Roma ho mangiato molto gelato, ogni giorno! Grazie per il biscotto. Tu ti piace Roma?

npc.narrative: The alba is clear sopra the tavolo, where Lazlo has laid out tre moduli and un biscotto. He stamps the first with the nuovo timbro, then joins a coda behind it, since there is nobody else, and waits piano.
npc.native: Gelato ogni giorno, che bell'idea! Sì, Roma mi piace molto, perché ha molte code ordinate. Io amo una coda. Quale gelato ti piace di più?
npc.translation: Gelato every day, what a lovely idea! Yes, I like Rome very much, because it has many orderly queues. I love a queue. Which gelato do you like best?

player: Mi piace il gelato al cioccolato. Ma a Roma non ci sono code ordinate, è un caos!

npc.narrative: Lazlo sets down his penna and looks at you as if you had reported a crime. The alba is pale and clear over the tavolo, and behind him a coda of one person, himself, waits patiently for nothing. He considers the biscotto in his pocket and, for the moment, leaves it there.
npc.native: Cioccolato, un'ottima scelta! Senza code? Che orrore! Io faccio una coda anche da solo, qui, all'alba. Che cosa fai tu la mattina presto?
npc.translation: Chocolate, an excellent choice! Without queues? How horrible! I form a queue even alone, here, at dawn. What do you do early in the morning?

player: La mattina presto io dormo! Poi bevo un caffè. Va bene, devo andare. Arrivederci, Lazlo!

npc.narrative: The sole climbs over the piazza, and Lazlo is già standing in a coda of one. He writes your name on a modulo with the nuovo timbro, molto slowly, while the old one waits in a cassetto, guilty. The cielo is clear.
npc.native: Tu dormi e poi bevi un caffè, che vita ordinata! Io certifico tutto, in triplice copia, e il modulo è quasi pronto. Un momento, per favore. Dove vai adesso?
npc.translation: You sleep and then you drink a coffee, what an orderly life! I certify everything, in triplicate, and the form is almost ready. One moment, please. Where are you going now?
